summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson was admitted for monitoring after undergoing his third transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) procedure for hepatocellular carcinoma. He tolerated the procedure well but developed expected post-embolization symptoms including right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and a significant transient elevation in liver enzymes. He also experienced temporary urinary retention requiring a straight catheterization, which resolved. His chronic conditions—alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis, thrombocytopenia, and ulcerative colitis—were managed throughout the stay. Liver function tests peaked but began to improve, and symptoms were controlled with supportive care. He was discharged home in stable condition with updated medications and follow-up plans.
